A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original sampling experiments on Ising/Potts and discretised synthetic distributions, Schrödinger bridge experiments, and MNIST latent-space posterior sampling.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds masking and gradient-detachment studies, computational-cost results, and LEAPS comparisons.

M1.justification: Appendix D.1.5 adds an evaluated training variant that backpropagates through only a subset of trajectory transition logits. The main TB/LV objectives, replay and MCMC strategies, bridge algorithms, and model architectures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Ising/Potts models, discretised 40GMM/ManyWell targets, synthetic bridge problems, and MNIST latent posterior tasks. The added experiments reuse existing targets without introducing new task requirements or populations.

E2.justification: v1 explicitly excludes LEAPS from benchmarking in Appendix C.1.2. v2 adds LEAPS comparisons on 16×16 Ising at beta=0.6 and Potts at beta=1.2 in Table 13. Existing benchmark comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments on 32-dimensional 40GMM vary inference unmaskings per step across 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16, and detached-logit fractions across 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 0.875 with fixed training-step budgets. Existing benchmark protocols and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis of computational tradeoffs: Appendices D.1.4–D.1.5 test inference masking schedules and partial-trajectory gradient computation, while D.1.6 compares computational costs. These supplement the retained annealing, off-policy-ratio, and MCMC-choice analyses.

E5.justification: Table 13 introduces mean±standard-deviation reporting over three runs for LEAPS, explicitly distinguished from five runs for the other methods. Existing five-run results and uncertainty-reporting conventions are unchanged.

E6.justification: Retained result tables are numerically unchanged, but Tables 10–13 add substantive sensitivity, cost, and comparator results. For example, TB + Buffer + MCMC has Sinkhorn distance 4.25±0.30 with one inference unmasking versus 30.11±1.94 with sixteen. Newly reported LEAPS Sinkhorn scores are 6.42±0.12 on Ising and 107.27±1.16 on Potts in Table 13.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 corrects the stated nonbinary uniform-diffusion kernel: a changed entry has C−1 alternatives, and its probability changes from p_flip/C to p_flip/(C−1), fixing normalization. The principal mathematical framework and derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about off-policy discrete sampling, data-to-energy discrete Schrödinger bridges, and posterior sampling in discrete latent spaces.

C2.justification: v2 proposes that simultaneous unmasking mitigates TB mode collapse by removing dependencies and attributes gradient-detachment degradation to slower convergence. Some new interpretation conflicts with results: D.1.4 calls an increasing Sinkhorn distance a decrease, and D.1.7 broadly describes LEAPS as worse on Potts although it beats TB + Buffer on Sinkhorn, 107.27 versus 156.12.

D1.justification: New Appendix C.3/Table 6 supplies bridge architecture, separate forward/backward learning rates, iteration counts, and buffer/MCMC settings for existing experiments. Appendices D.1.6–D.1.7 add energy-evaluation counts, approximate runtimes, and H100 hardware information. The code link points to the same repository.

R1.justification: New Section 6 expands discussion of amortised sampling, discrete diffusion, and Schrödinger bridges while retaining the original positioning. Added references include Avdeyev et al. (2023), Tong et al. (2024), and Venkatraman et al. (2024), the latter supporting partial-gradient training.

P1.justification: The bridge subsection becomes a standalone section, a Related Work section and Impact Statement are added, and appendix explanations and cross-references expand. Most existing prose, including the abstract and conclusion, remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds bridge-hyperparameter Table 6 and experimental Tables 10–13. Existing displays are repositioned, including Figures 4 and 5 appearing side by side, while their visual content and the basic document layout are preserved.

improvement.justification: The LEAPS comparison, computational-tradeoff studies, and newly disclosed bridge settings improve empirical support and reproducibility; Appendix A.2 also fixes a kernel formula. These are useful additions to an otherwise stable paper. Incorrect Sinkhorn-direction wording and an overbroad LEAPS interpretation temper the gains, but do not outweigh the added evidence.
